children.label: a
children.prompt: Given three points $A$, $B$ and $C$ with position vectors $\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\end{pmatrix}$, $\begin{pmatrix}4\\-1\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}k\\-7\end{pmatrix}$ respectively, find the value of $k$ such that $\overrightarrow{AB}$ is parallel to $\overrightarrow{BC}$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AB}&=\begin{pmatrix}4\\-1\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}3\\-3\end{pmatrix}\\\overrightarrow{BC}&=\begin{pmatrix}k\\-7\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}4\\-1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}k-4\\-6\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}$$
For parallel vectors, the scalar multiple is $2$ because $-6=2\times(-3)$.
$$\begin{aligned}k-4&=2\times3\\k&=10\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Given three points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ with position vectors $\begin{pmatrix}3\\5\end{pmatrix}$, $\begin{pmatrix}-1\\k\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}5\\-4\end{pmatrix}$ respectively, find the value of $k$ such that $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ is parallel to $\overrightarrow{PR}$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{PQ}&=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\k\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}3\\5\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-4\\k-5\end{pmatrix}\\\overrightarrow{PR}&=\begin{pmatrix}5\\-4\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}3\\5\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\-9\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}$$
For parallel vectors, the scalar multiple is $-2$ because $-4=-2\times2$.
$$\begin{aligned}k-5&=-2\times(-9)\\k-5&=18\\k&=23\end{aligned}$$

children.label: a
children.prompt:
$\overrightarrow{AB}=3\underset{\sim}{a}-2\underset{\sim}{b}$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}=6\underset{\sim}{a}+4\underset{\sim}{b}$.

Show that $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}$ are not parallel.

answer.short: Matching coefficients gives $k=2$ and $k=-2$, so the vectors are not parallel.
answer.worked:
If parallel, $\overrightarrow{CD}=k\overrightarrow{AB}$.
$$\begin{align*}6\underset{\sim}{a}+4\underset{\sim}{b}&=k(3\underset{\sim}{a}-2\underset{\sim}{b})\\&=3k\underset{\sim}{a}-2k\underset{\sim}{b}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{a}:\quad 6&=3k\Rightarrow k=2\\\underset{\sim}{b}:\quad 4&=-2k\Rightarrow k=-2\end{align*}$$
The values of $k$ differ, so $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}$ are not parallel.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
$\overrightarrow{AB}=3\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}=\underset{\sim}{a}-4\underset{\sim}{b}$.

Show that $\overrightarrow{AC}$ is not parallel to $\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b}$.

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{AC}=4\underset{\sim}{a}-3\underset{\sim}{b}$; matching coefficients gives $k=4$ and $k=3$, so it is not parallel.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{AC}&=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}\\&=(3\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b})+(\underset{\sim}{a}-4\underset{\sim}{b})\\&=4\underset{\sim}{a}-3\underset{\sim}{b}\end{align*}$$
If parallel, $\overrightarrow{AC}=k(\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b})=k\underset{\sim}{a}-k\underset{\sim}{b}$.
$$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{a}:\quad 4&=k\\\underset{\sim}{b}:\quad -3&=-k\Rightarrow k=3\end{align*}$$
The values of $k$ differ, so $\overrightarrow{AC}$ is not parallel to $\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt:
$\overrightarrow{PQ}=\tfrac12\underset{\sim}{a}+2\underset{\sim}{b}$ and $\overrightarrow{RS}=3\underset{\sim}{a}+8\underset{\sim}{b}$.

Show that $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ and $\overrightarrow{RS}$ are not parallel.

answer.short: Matching coefficients gives $k=6$ and $k=4$, so the vectors are not parallel.
answer.worked:
If parallel, $\overrightarrow{RS}=k\overrightarrow{PQ}$.
$$\begin{align*}3\underset{\sim}{a}+8\underset{\sim}{b}&=k(\tfrac12\underset{\sim}{a}+2\underset{\sim}{b})\\&=\tfrac12k\underset{\sim}{a}+2k\underset{\sim}{b}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{a}:\quad 3&=\tfrac12k\Rightarrow k=6\\\underset{\sim}{b}:\quad 8&=2k\Rightarrow k=4\end{align*}$$
The values of $k$ differ, so $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ and $\overrightarrow{RS}$ are not parallel.

payloads.replacement:
**Parallelogram law of subtraction**

$$\overrightarrow{AB}-\overrightarrow{AD}=\overrightarrow{DB}$$

When two vectors start from the same point, their difference is the vector from the head of the second vector to the head of the first.

Two non-zero vectors $\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b}$ are **parallel** if they have the **same direction** or **opposite directions**.

In other words, one vector is a non-zero scalar multiple of the other.

$\underset{\sim}{b}=\lambda\underset{\sim}{a},\qquad\lambda\in\mathbb{R},\ \lambda\neq0$
